prompt:
Write the appraiser's remarks (about 80 words) on a body shop repair estimate after a low-speed head-on collision. Describe the damage seen on the vehicle and the repair plan. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1056; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The bills show no repeated charges.
- The repair labor hours are a little high for this damage.
- A few old scratches may be older than this crash.
text: The vehicle presents front-end damage consistent with the reported low-speed head-on impact, including a cracked bumper cover, a bent upper radiator support, and a displaced hood latch. The repair plan calls for replacing the bumper cover and hood latch, straightening the support, and refinishing the affected panels. Shop invoices reviewed so far show no duplicated line items. Labor hours appear slightly high for the extent of this damage and should be checked against the standard time guide. A few older scratches on the lower door area may predate this incident and should be noted separately from the repair scope.
